  • Parent size derives automatically from the packed children plus SetGroupPadding()

It covers HDR and wide gamut up to 32-bit float per channel, alpha, animation and any number of extra channels. Reading the chart\n\nEach bar's width is:
Reading the chart

Each bar's width is its share of the top stage, so the taper is the funnel.

The pale neck between two bars carries the conversion from the upper stage into the lower one - 68.22% of everyone who was sent the mail opened it.

The right-hand column is a different figure: the share of the very first stage, so it always falls monotonically.

Where the funnel leaks

  - The worst step is Clicked to Add to Cart at 36.57%.
  - Once a basket exists the funnel barely leaks at all: 92.62% check out.
  - End to end, 9.95% of recipients buy.

Hover any bar for the raw count, both percentages and the number lost at that step.
Reading the chart\n\nThe tiers are area-:
Reading the chart

The tiers are area-proportional, which is the setting that makes a pyramid honest. A pyramid's sides taper, so a band's area grows faster than its height: sizing tiers by height alone quietly overstates every tier near the base.

Solving for the cut position instead means the ink a reader sees is the quantity the data actually holds.

The reference shape

The dashed silhouette and its rules are the 70/20/10 split the team is aiming for. Read the gap between the drawn cut and the dashed one - that is the distance from the target, per tier.

This suite is off target: 6,540 tests split 63% unit, 19% integration and 18% end to end. Every dashed rule sits above the tier boundary it belongs to, which is the shape saying there is too much at the top.

Top-heavy warning

SetHighlightTopHeavy outlines the first tier that outweighs the one holding it up - the ice-cream-cone suite. Every tier here is larger than the one above it, so nothing is flagged - the suite is badly proportioned, not upside down.
